gloss: grasp all, lose all; falling between two stools

definitions.gloss: failing to get either by trying to get both
definitions.explanation: A proverb warning against trying to pursue two goals at once and ending up with neither. Similar to 'falling between two stools.'

examples.japanese: ⟦{二|ふた}つ→二つ：02953_futatsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{同時|どうじ}→同時：01592_douji⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦やろう→やる：02980_yaru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧{虻|あぶ}{蜂|はち}{取|と}らず⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: I tried to do two jobs at once and ended up failing at both.

examples.japanese: ⟦{欲張|よくば}る→欲張る：15774_yokubaru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{虻|あぶ}{蜂|はち}{取|と}らず⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
examples.english: If you're too greedy, you'll end up with nothing.

examples.japanese: {虻|あぶ}{蜂|はち}{取|と}らず⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ならない→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦ように→ように：10081_youni⟧、⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{集中|しゅうちゅう}→集中：03212_shuuchuu⟧⟦しよう→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Let's focus on one thing so we don't end up with neither.

notes:
PROVERB MEANING:
Literally: 'Catching neither the horsefly nor the bee.' The image is of someone trying to catch both a horsefly (⟦{虻|あぶ}→虻：24997_abu⟧) and a bee (⟦{蜂|はち}→蜂：02242_hachi⟧) at the same time, but failing to catch either one.

ETYMOLOGY:
This proverb comes from the idea that if you're distracted trying to get multiple things, you'll lose focus and miss all of them.

USAGE:
Used as a warning against greed, divided attention, or trying to pursue too many goals simultaneously.

ENGLISH EQUIVALENTS:
- Grasp all, lose all
- Fall between two stools
- A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush (similar theme)
- Between two stools, one falls to the ground

SIMILAR JAPANESE EXPRESSIONS:
- {二兎|にと}を{追|お}う{者|もの}は{一兎|いっと}をも{得|え}ず: He who chases two rabbits catches neither
